independence_declaration.statement: qa-verifier authored no product implementation in the DG2 scope. Its only authored files are QA tests, harnesses and evidence (tests/qa/**, e2e/**, docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/qa/**). The round-13 repair (D-073: BE18A 8c0083e by backend-workflow-engineer) is not mine. Every result here comes from qa-verifier's own runs in three disposable clones under $TMPDIR, all removed at the end. Two clones are at 5699f72, the round-13 freeze on top of source aa0a68f1. The third, at the round-12 freeze 744af0b, was used only for the negative control. At the start HEAD was 5699f72, not the source commit aa0a68f1. aa0a68f1..5699f72 is a single orchestrator freeze commit that changes only the three round-13 assignments, the candidate manifest and stages.json, all outside the manifest. The recomputed candidate ID is sha256:6824b8b8... (556 files) both in the tree and at --ref aa0a68f1, and --diff matches with no added, removed or changed files. During the run HEAD moved to 2f8a11c through the other reviewers' auto-committed round-13 evidence and a round-14 assignment commit. I did not open those files; I saw only their commit subjects and file names in git (00-candidate-end.log). At the end the candidate ID was still 6824b8b8... with 556 files. My verdict was formed from my own runs, without reading any other reviewer's round-13 record.

checks_run.procedure: Read the BE18A fix statically: the shutdown order in main.ts, the tracker's registration order and coverage, and the sweep's name, depth, symlink and mtime rules.

checks_run.actual: main.ts awaits app.close(), then inFlight.settled(SHUTDOWN_SETTLE_MS = 3000) (it warns if not settled), then db.destroy(), then process.exit(0). The backstop is grace + 5 s = 10 s, exiting 1. registerInFlightTracking is at server.ts:232, before helmet, cookie, rate-limit, health, the modules and static, so every route is tracked. denials.ts tracks the failed-mutation audit, and the evidence onReady hook tracks the sweep. The sweep requires TEMPORARY_NAME (lowercase UUID + .part), KEY_DEPTH 3, Dirent isDirectory/isFile (false for links), an lstat re-check and age over STALE_TEMPORARY_AGE_MS (1 h). receive() now removes the temporary in a finally block even when handle.close() fails. This agrees with the dynamic results.

checks_run.procedure: New R13-04 (D-073 regression, my own negative checks over real sockets against the real stack). (a) Positive control: dev.nobody gets a KDS team assignment through POST /transformations/{t}/scoped-assignments and uploads their own file evidence. (b) That only grant is revoked through POST /role-assignments/{id}/revoke (dev.admin) while the body streams. (b2) A team assignment whose effectiveTo (6 s ahead) passes while the body streams, with the session still valid. (c) The uploading session logs out (POST /auth/logout) while the body streams; the same user's other session is checked afterwards.
checks_run.expected: (a) 200, byte-exact, sha256 = DB. (b) The session has ended at commit, so 401 unauthenticated, nothing stored. (b2) 403 forbidden, audited authorization.denied, nothing stored, the session still works. (c) 401 unauthenticated, nothing stored, the other session unaffected. Item versions are unchanged in every refusal.
checks_run.actual: Passed 4 of 4. (a) 200, download byte-exact, DB = sha256. (b) The revoke returned 200 with revokedAt set, and the upload got 401 unauthenticated. The product's revoke also revokes the member's session rows (count above 0; after it, the member's GET /me is 401), so the commit-time re-resolution correctly finds no session. Content rows 0, store [], item version/current '1 null' unchanged. (b2) 403 forbidden; the audit actions for the request are exactly 'authorization.denied'; content rows 0, store [], item unchanged; the session's GET /me afterwards is 200. (c) logout 200, then the upload gets 401 unauthenticated; content rows 0, store [], item v1->v1; the logged-out session's /me is 401 and the user's other session's /me is 200. Note on my first development run (18-r13-spec-dev-run1.log, exit 1): I had expected 403 for case (b). A separate probe (audit 'scoped_assignment.revoke' then 'session.revoke'; the member's active sessions went 1 to 0) showed the revoke ends the session by design ('Takes effect for the next request'). I corrected the expectation to 401 and added (b2) for the 403 path. Nothing was stored in any variant.

summary: PASS on candidate 6824b8b8 (556 files, source aa0a68f1). F-DG2-460 is CLOSED_VERIFIED. My round-12 reproductions R12-07 and R11-02 now pass 4 of 4 (en/ar × both locale settings): nothing is stored after SIGTERM and the process exits 0. The new R13-01 test (two uploads actively streaming through the whole grace, plus a stalled one) leaves no .part and no final object, exits 0 in about 5.03 s, logs no settle warning and no error line, and a restart finds nothing. R13-02 shows an upload that finishes inside the grace still commits byte-exact. R13-03 shows the start-up sweep removes and logs only the stale <uuid>.part and keeps fresh and near-threshold temporaries, all final objects, look-alikes, wrong-depth files, directories and symlinked paths. A negative control on the pre-fix freeze 744af0b fails those probes, as designed. D-073 regression: an upload whose grant is revoked through the API gets 401 (the revoke also ends the session); a grant that expires mid-upload gets 403, audited as authorization.denied; a logout mid-upload gets 401. Nothing is stored in any of these cases. 25 logins against a never-answering IdP hold no transaction. Binary, Unicode and R8-05/R9-05 still pass. Static checks are all exit 0 (161 operations). Unit: 7 of 7 runs, 796 tests each. Integration: 6 of 6 runs, 652 tests each. Product e2e: 64 of 64 per setting. QA-stack e2e: 142 of 142 per setting. axe: 636 scans with 0 violations. The validators pass. The residuals D-057, D-058 and D-049 pass on the offline/config surface; the residuals themselves remain. No new findings. No business approval is implied; product gates G1–G6 are separate from DG0–DG7.
